intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Begin your mornings with a guided yoga session at the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud. This serene hilltop setting offers panoramic views of lush green valleys and is ideal for yoga practitioners of all levels. Since the flight arrives late on Day 1, this activity is perfectly suited for Day 2 onwards, allowing you to ease into the trip with a mindful morning ritual close to Ubud's central accommodation hubs.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Beachfront Dining
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon on Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most accessible and vibrant beach strips. Enjoy swimming, sunbathing, and watching the famous Bali sunset. Follow it up with a beachfront dinner at one of the many affordable warungs or mid-range restaurants nearby. Seminyak is a central hub with many hotels, making this a convenient and cost-effective experience requiring no long travel.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Local Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a half-day cooking class based in central Ubud that starts with a guided tour of a traditional local market. Learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes such as satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding using fresh local ingredients. This experience is centrally located in Ubud, close to major accommodation areas, and is a perfect Day 2 afternoon activity after arriving late the night before.

experiences.name: Tirta Empul Temple & Sacred Water Purification
experiences.description: Visit the sacred Tirta Empul Temple, a UNESCO-recognized cultural site where locals and visitors participate in a traditional Hindu purification ritual in natural spring pools. This deeply spiritual and culturally immersive experience is located just 15 minutes from central Ubud, making it easily accessible without long transfers. Pair it with a visit to the nearby Tegallalang Rice Terraces for a full cultural day.

experiences.name: Stand-Up Paddleboarding at Sanur Beach
experiences.description: Sanur Beach offers calm, shallow waters perfect for stand-up paddleboarding (SUP), making it ideal for beginners and yoga enthusiasts looking to complement their practice with a water-based activity. Sanur is well-connected to both Seminyak and Ubud, and its calm reef-protected waters ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. Lessons and board rentals are affordable and widely available along the beachfront promenade.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport shuttle or shared Grab car to Ubud Boutique Stay (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along Jalan Monkey Forest to get oriented with the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ubud Night Market (Pasar Malam Ubud) on Jalan Raya Ubud for an introduction to local street food. Browse handcraft stalls and soak up the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite at the airport or a warung near the hotel after check-in (nasi campur ~IDR 25,000).
meals.dinner: Ubud Night Market street food — satay, martabak, and fresh fruit for under IDR 50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Download the Grab app before landing for cheap ride-hailing. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport kiosk for immediate needs; better rates are available at money changers in Ubud.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or donation-based sunrise yoga class at Yoga Barn Ubud (community class ~IDR 100,000) or practice on your hotel terrace. Afterward, walk the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk — a flat, breezy trail above the river valley, completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and the adjacent Ubud Art Market for budget souvenir shopping. Browse handwoven textiles, wood carvings, and silver jewellery — bargaining is expected.
day_by_day.evening: Watch a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud (tickets ~IDR 100,000). Return to the hotel on foot — the venue is within walking distance.

meals.breakfast: Warung Biah Biah or hotel breakfast if included — nasi goreng and fresh juice (~IDR 35,000).
meals.lunch: Warung Ibu Oka for budget babi guling (suckling pig rice) ~IDR 50,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Teges near the palace — local dishes from IDR 30,000–50,000.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light rain jacket; afternoon showers are possible even in the dry season. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the ridge walk.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~IDR 50,000/day) and cycle through the Tegallalang Rice Terraces — arrive early (before 08:30) to beat crowds and enjoy cooler temperatures. The terraces are about 8 km north of Ubud.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling to Gunung Kawi Temple (entry ~IDR 50,000 including sarong rental) — ancient rock-cut shrines set in a lush river valley. Spend 1–2 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes and relax at the hotel. Head to Jalan Dewisita for a quiet dinner at a local warung.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie bowl at a local café near the hotel (~IDR 40,000).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a warung near Tegallalang — nasi bungkus (wrapped rice) ~IDR 20,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Sopa — vegetarian-friendly local dishes ~IDR 40,000–60,000.

day_by_day.notes: The rice terrace path has an entry fee of IDR 10,000–15,000 at some access points. Cycling on Bali roads requires care — stick to quieter back roads where possible.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga session at The Yoga Barn (community class) or a free guided meditation at a local temple. Afterward, visit Tirta Empul Holy Spring Temple (~IDR 50,000 entry) for a purification ritual — a deeply spiritual and culturally immersive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bemo (local minibus) to Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave Temple, ~IDR 50,000). Explore the ancient cave shrine and surrounding jungle gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Gamelan music rehearsal at a community banjar (village hall) — ask your hotel for the nearest schedule. End the evening with a walk along Monkey Forest Road.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Kafe Kopi Bali for local coffee and banana pancakes (~IDR 35,000).
meals.lunch: Warung near Tirta Empul — mixed rice plate ~IDR 30,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka No. 2 or Naughty Nuri's Warung for budget ribs — ~IDR 60,000–80,000.

day_by_day.notes: A sarong is required at both temples — free to borrow at the entrance. Tirta Empul is best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mount Batur volcano area. Take a shared shuttle from Ubud (~IDR 50,000 each way). Hike the caldera rim trail with a local guide (budget guide ~IDR 150,000–200,000) for panoramic views of the lake and volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the natural hot springs at Toya Bungkah on the shores of Lake Batur (~IDR 50,000–100,000 entry). A perfect recovery after the morning hike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud by shared shuttle. Rest and enjoy a quiet evening on Jalan Raya Ubud.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab a banana and local coffee from a roadside stall (~IDR 10,000).
meals.lunch: Warung at Toya Bungkah lakeside — grilled corn, noodle soup ~IDR 35,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Makan Bu Rus in Ubud — hearty Balinese home cooking ~IDR 40,000.

day_by_day.notes: The Batur hike is best done in the morning when skies are clear. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. Note: this is a full-day excursion — budget ~IDR 400,000–500,000 all in.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — gentle yoga or stretching on the hotel terrace. Visit the Ubud Traditional Market early (before 09:00) for the freshest produce and best prices on spices, sarongs, and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend a free Balinese cooking demonstration at a local home kitchen or join a budget cooking class (~IDR 150,000–250,000) to learn to make tempeh satay, lawar, and black rice pudding.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Monkey Forest Sanctuary (Sacred Monkey Forest Ubud, ~IDR 80,000 entry) at dusk when it's less crowded. Watch hundreds of macaques settle in for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Fresh market fruit — papaya, rambutan, salak — bought at the market ~IDR 20,000.
meals.lunch: Eat your cooking class creations, or Warung Enak near Monkey Forest ~IDR 35,000.
meals.dinner: Clear Café Ubud — healthy, budget-friendly menu with vegetarian options ~IDR 60,000–80,000.

day_by_day.notes: Keep bags zipped and do not feed the monkeys at Monkey Forest. The market is most vibrant between 06:00–09:00.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: check out of Ubud Boutique Stay and take a shared shuttle or Grab to Seminyak/Canggu area (approx. 1.5 hrs, ~IDR 80,000–120,000). Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in Canggu (~IDR 150,000–250,000/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head straight to Batu Bolong Beach or Echo Beach in Canggu — both free to access. Swim, sunbathe, and watch surfers tackle the famous reef breaks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Canggu's trendy but budget-friendly café strip along Jalan Pantai Batu Bolong. Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Bali's finest free experiences.

meals.breakfast: Quick nasi goreng at a Ubud warung before departure ~IDR 25,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Batu Bolong Beach — grilled fish with rice ~IDR 45,000.
meals.dinner: Old Man's Bar & Restaurant (happy hour deals) or a local warung on the beach strip ~IDR 50,000–70,000.

day_by_day.notes: Canggu has strong rip currents — swim between the flags and heed lifeguard warnings. Renting a scooter here (~IDR 70,000/day) is the most budget-efficient way to explore the area.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga at Desa Seni Yoga Studio in Canggu (community class ~IDR 120,000) or a free beach yoga session at Pererenan Beach. Afterward, rent a surfboard (~IDR 50,000–80,000/hr with instructor) for a beginner surf lesson at Batu Bolong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scooter ride to Tanah Lot Temple (approx. 20 min from Canggu, entry ~IDR 60,000) — a dramatic sea temple perched on a coastal rock. Walk the clifftop paths and explore the temple grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Canggu for sunset. Browse the Canggu Club area and enjoy a cheap Bintang beer at a beachside warung.

meals.breakfast: Warung Dandelion or a smoothie bowl café in Canggu ~IDR 45,000–55,000.
meals.lunch: Warung near Tanah Lot — nasi campur ~IDR 30,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Sunset Road — local Balinese food with rice and sambal ~IDR 40,000.

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is most scenic at low tide and around sunset — check tide times before visiting. The temple inner sanctum is only accessible to Hindu worshippers.

day_by_day.morning: Early scooter trip to Seminyak Beach (15 min from Canggu). Walk the long stretch of black-sand beach south toward Kuta. Visit Pura Petitenget — a peaceful seaside temple with beautiful architecture (free entry, sarong required).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Kuta Beach — Bali's most famous stretch of sand. Swim in the warm water, rent a sun lounger (~IDR 30,000), or try bodyboarding (~IDR 50,000/hr). Walk the full length of Kuta Beach toward Legian.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kuta's famous night scene on a budget — skip the clubs and enjoy cheap cocktails at a beach bar. Watch fire dancers perform on the beach (free, tips appreciated).

meals.breakfast: Local warung in Seminyak — bubur ayam (chicken porridge) ~IDR 25,000.
meals.lunch: Warung 64 in Kuta — generous portions of local food ~IDR 35,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Poppies Lane II in Kuta — famous for budget local restaurants, meal ~IDR 45,000–65,000.

day_by_day.notes: Kuta can feel overwhelming — keep valuables secure and be aware of beach vendors. The beach is best in the morning before it gets crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Bukit Peninsula. Scooter south to Uluwatu Temple (entry ~IDR 50,000) — dramatically perched 70m above the Indian Ocean on sheer limestone cliffs. Arrive by 08:30 for the best light and fewest crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Padang Padang Beach (~IDR 15,000 entry) — a hidden cove accessed through a narrow cave, with crystal-clear water perfect for snorkelling. Alternatively, visit Bingin Beach for a more secluded experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Uluwatu for the famous Kecak Fire Dance at sunset (tickets ~IDR 100,000) performed in the temple's clifftop amphitheatre — one of Bali's most spectacular free-sunset backdrops.

meals.breakfast: Café near Canggu guesthouse — eggs and toast ~IDR 35,000.
meals.lunch: Warung at Padang Padang Beach — fresh coconut and nasi goreng ~IDR 40,000.
meals.dinner: Single Fin Bar & Restaurant at Uluwatu — budget-friendly menu with ocean views ~IDR 70,000–90,000.

day_by_day.notes: Monkeys at Uluwatu are notorious for snatching sunglasses, hats, and phones — hold belongings tightly. The Kecak performance starts at 18:00 — arrive 30 min early for good seats.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga on Canggu beach or at a drop-in studio. Then scooter to Pererenan or Seseh Beach — quieter, less touristy black-sand beaches north of Canggu, ideal for a peaceful morning swim and meditation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pura Dalem Petitenget or explore the rice paddies of Berawa on foot. Stop at a local warung for a traditional jamu herbal drink (~IDR 10,000). Visit a traditional Balinese healer (balian) if interested — ask your guesthouse for a trusted referral.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Berawa Beach followed by dinner at a beachside warung. Enjoy live acoustic music that many Canggu bars host for free on weekday evenings.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl at Betelnut Café or a local warung ~IDR 40,000–50,000.
meals.lunch: Warung in Pererenan village — home-cooked nasi campur ~IDR 25,000.
meals.dinner: Warung Sunset Canggu — grilled fish, tempeh, and rice ~IDR 50,000.

day_by_day.notes: This is a slower, more reflective day — ideal for journaling, reading, or a budget massage (~IDR 80,000–100,000/hr at a local spa).

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — head to Seminyak Beach for a long swim and last surf session. Rent a board for one final ride (~IDR 80,000/hr). Take photos and collect any last-minute souvenirs from the Seminyak markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bali's famous Seminyak Square or Oberoi Street for window shopping. Stop at a local spa for a traditional Balinese massage — budget spas charge ~IDR 80,000–120,000 for a full-body hour. Return to guesthouse to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Canggu or Seminyak. Splurge slightly on a nicer warung for a memorable last meal. Watch the final Bali sunset from the beach with a fresh coconut in hand.

meals.breakfast: Warung in Canggu — full Balinese breakfast with coffee ~IDR 35,000.
meals.lunch: Warung Murah in Seminyak — famous for generous, cheap local food ~IDR 30,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Merah Putih or a mid-range warung for a slightly special farewell meal ~IDR 80,000–120,000.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer for the next morning. Exchange remaining IDR back to your home currency at a reputable money changer in Seminyak before leaving.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up and final packing. Enjoy a last local breakfast near the guesthouse. Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (~30 min from Canggu by Grab or pre-booked shuttle ~IDR 100,000–150,000). Allow at least 3 hours before international departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport check-in, security, and departure. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Bali coffee, chocolate, or spice souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — reflect on 13 wonderful days in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Final nasi goreng or bubur ayam at a warung near the guesthouse ~IDR 25,000.
meals.lunch: Airport food court — local options available at reasonable prices ~IDR 50,000–80,000.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Bali's airport can be busy — arrive early. Keep a small amount of IDR for any last-minute tips or airport fees. Estimated total trip budget (excluding flights): IDR 3,500,000–5,000,000 (~USD 215–310) for 13 days including accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer to Ubud Boutique Stay (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along Monkey Forest Road to get oriented with the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ubud's vibrant night scene on Jalan Hanoman. Browse local art shops and settle into the Balinese atmosphere with a relaxed walk through the town centre.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a light bite at the airport or a warungs (local eatery) near the hotel upon arrival — try nasi campur (mixed rice) for around IDR 30,000–50,000.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — famous for Balinese suckling pig; budget approx. IDR 80,000–120,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Hydrate well and adjust to the warm, humid climate. Exchange currency at a reputable money changer in Ubud rather than the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a sunrise yoga class at one of Ubud's renowned yoga studios, such as Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive. A 90-minute morning flow class costs approx. IDR 150,000–200,000. Return to the hotel for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (entry approx. IDR 80,000). Wander through the ancient temple grounds and lush jungle paths. Afterward, explore the Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for handmade crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — tickets approx. IDR 100,000–150,000. A mesmerising cultural experience set in an open-air royal courtyard.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try a smoothie bowl and eggs at Kafe Ubud (IDR 60,000–90,000).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Warung Teges — authentic Balinese dishes at local prices (IDR 40,000–70,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Locavore To Go or Naughty Nuri's Warung — wood-fired ribs and cocktails; budget IDR 120,000–200,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kecak Dance in advance or ask the hotel concierge. Wear a sarong to enter temple areas — many can be rented at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or join a guided cycling tour through Ubud's countryside. Ride through rice paddies, traditional villages, and past the Campuhan Ridge Walk trail. A guided cycling tour costs approx. IDR 250,000–350,000 including breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tirta Empul Temple — a sacred Hindu water temple famous for its purification rituals in holy spring water (entry approx. IDR 50,000). Participate respectfully in the melukat purification ritual if comfortable.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a traditional Balinese massage at a reputable spa in Ubud, such as COMO Shambhala or Taksu Spa. A 60-minute massage costs IDR 200,000–350,000.

meals.breakfast: Included with the cycling tour — typically a traditional Balinese breakfast with rice, vegetables, and fruit.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a warung near Tirta Empul — try sate lilit (Balinese fish satay) and fresh coconut water (IDR 50,000–80,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bridges Bali — a stunning restaurant perched over the Campuhan River gorge; mid-range menu IDR 150,000–250,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a change of clothes and a waterproof bag if participating in the Tirta Empul water ritual. Light rain is possible in the afternoon — carry a compact umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin Yoga or meditation session at Yoga Barn (IDR 150,000). Afterward, visit the Ubud Palace and surrounding streets for a peaceful morning walk before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Tegalalang Rice Terraces (approx. 20 mins from Ubud by scooter or taxi). Walk the iconic stepped terraces, take photos, and enjoy the scenic viewpoints. Entry donation approx. IDR 15,000–30,000. Visit a nearby coffee plantation for a Luwak coffee tasting (IDR 50,000–80,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud and browse the night market near Ubud Traditional Market for local snacks and street food.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Seniman Coffee Studio — specialty coffee and avocado toast (IDR 70,000–100,000).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sari Organik — a farm-to-table restaurant nestled in the rice fields near Tegalalang (IDR 80,000–130,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hujan Locale — modern Indonesian cuisine with a curated menu (IDR 150,000–220,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hire a scooter (IDR 70,000–100,000/day) or use a Grab/Gojek ride-share app for easy transport. Tegalalang is busiest mid-morning — arrive before 10:00 or after 15:00 for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise trek to Mount Batur (Gunung Batur) — depart from Ubud around 02:00 with a guided group. Summit at sunrise for breathtaking panoramic views over the caldera and Lake Batur. Trek duration approx. 4–5 hours round trip. Cost: IDR 350,000–500,000 including guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ubud by early afternoon. Rest and recover at the hotel. Optional: soak in a natural hot spring near Mount Batur before heading back (entry IDR 50,000–100,000).
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening in Ubud. Gentle stroll and early dinner.

meals.breakfast: Simple snacks and hot tea provided at the Mount Batur base camp before the trek.
meals.lunch: Late lunch / brunch at the hotel or a nearby café — try a fresh açaí bowl or Balinese rice dish.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Warung Ibu Oka 2 — local Balinese comfort food; budget IDR 60,000–100,000.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Mount Batur trek through your hotel or a trusted operator at least 1–2 days in advance. Bring warm layers, a headlamp, and sturdy shoes — temperatures at the summit can drop to 10–15°C before dawn.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — attend a gentle restorative yoga class at Radiantly Alive (IDR 150,000). Take it easy and enjoy a slow morning in Ubud.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Agung Rai Museum of Art (ARMA) — one of Bali's finest art museums showcasing traditional and contemporary Balinese art (entry IDR 80,000). Explore the lush garden grounds and catch a cultural performance if scheduled.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Legong Dance performance at ARMA or Ubud Palace — a classical Balinese dance featuring intricate costumes and storytelling (tickets IDR 100,000–150,000).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Kopi Desa — a charming café with local-style breakfast sets (IDR 50,000–80,000).
meals.lunch: Lunch at ARMA's on-site restaurant — Indonesian and Western options in a beautiful garden setting (IDR 100,000–160,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique — a splurge-worthy fine dining experience with French-Indonesian fusion (IDR 400,000–700,000 per person; book in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally slower to recover from the Batur trek. The Mozaic dinner is an optional splurge — substitute with a mid-range warung if preferred to stay on budget.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Ubud to Seminyak / Canggu area (approx. 1.5 hrs by private driver — IDR 200,000–300,000). Check in or drop bags at a day-use arrangement, then head straight to the beach. Enjoy the black-sand beaches of Canggu — Echo Beach or Batu Bolong Beach are ideal for a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a surfboard and take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson at Canggu Surf School (IDR 250,000–400,000 for 2-hour lesson). The warm July waves are excellent for surfing.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rock formation (entry IDR 60,000). Arrive 1 hour before sunset for the best views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Ubud before departing — grab a takeaway from Bali Buda (IDR 50,000–80,000).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside warung in Canggu — fresh grilled fish, nasi goreng, or a smoothie bowl (IDR 60,000–100,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Brisa Bali — a stunning beachfront restaurant in Echo Beach with fresh seafood (IDR 150,000–250,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the Ubud–Canggu transfer and Tanah Lot visit — this can often be bundled for a flat rate. If staying in Ubud for the full trip, this can be done as a day trip returning in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach yoga session on Seminyak Beach — many resorts and instructors offer open-air classes at sunrise (IDR 100,000–150,000). Follow with a refreshing swim in the warm Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seminyak's boutique shopping strip along Jalan Kayu Aya. Browse designer homeware, fashion, and local craft shops. Visit Ku De Ta beach club for a relaxed afternoon by the pool or beach (no entry fee; minimum spend applies).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Seminyak Beach — one of the best sunset spots in Bali. Enjoy cocktails at a beachside bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Sisterfields Café in Seminyak — popular for eggs benedict and specialty coffee (IDR 80,000–130,000).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Warung Nia — a beloved local spot for authentic Balinese food at affordable prices (IDR 50,000–90,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merah Putih — a stunning restaurant in a dramatic open-air space serving modern Indonesian cuisine (IDR 200,000–350,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is more upscale than Canggu — budget slightly more for dining and activities here. Taxis and ride-shares are readily available.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Uluwatu — travel approx. 45 mins south by driver. Visit Uluwatu Temple (Pura Luhur Uluwatu) perched dramatically on a 70-metre clifftop above the ocean (entry IDR 50,000). Watch for monkeys and enjoy the stunning coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Padang Padang Beach or Bingin Beach — two of Bali's most beautiful and secluded beaches. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on the white sand (entry IDR 20,000–30,000).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset — widely regarded as the most spectacular setting for this performance (tickets IDR 150,000). Return to Seminyak/Canggu or Ubud by private driver.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local café before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Single Fin — a legendary cliff-top café and bar in Uluwatu with panoramic ocean views (IDR 100,000–180,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ulu Cliffhouse or a warung near the beach — fresh seafood BBQ at sunset (IDR 100,000–200,000).

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Uluwatu day trip — IDR 350,000–500,000 for the full day including all stops. Wear a sarong at Uluwatu Temple; they are provided at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Ubud (if you've been based in the south) or enjoy a morning yoga class at Yoga Barn. Visit the Campuhan Ridge Walk — a scenic 2 km trail through lush green hills just outside Ubud town. Best done early morning before the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Balinese cooking class — learn to prepare traditional dishes like satay, lawar, and black rice pudding. Classes run approx. 3–4 hours and include a market visit; cost IDR 300,000–500,000 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as dinner, or head out to a favourite Ubud restaurant for a celebratory meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Café Pomegranate — healthy bowls and fresh juices (IDR 60,000–90,000).
meals.lunch: Light lunch included as part of the cooking class experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Locavore — one of Bali's top farm-to-table restaurants; book well in advance (IDR 400,000–600,000 per person for the tasting menu).

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2 days in advance. Popular options include Paon Bali Cooking Class and Casa Luna Cooking School. The Campuhan Ridge Walk is best before 08:00 to avoid heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Besakih Temple — Bali's largest and most sacred Mother Temple located on the slopes of Mount Agung (approx. 1.5 hrs from Ubud). Entry IDR 60,000. Hire a local guide for context and to navigate the complex (IDR 100,000–150,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Sidemen Valley on the return journey — one of Bali's most scenic and untouched areas. Walk through terraced rice fields and visit a traditional weaving village where artisans craft ikat textiles by hand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud for a relaxing evening. Book a traditional Javanese or Balinese spa treatment — a 90-minute package at a mid-range spa costs IDR 250,000–400,000.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local warung in Sidemen — simple, fresh Balinese food with stunning rice field views (IDR 40,000–70,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Warung Babi Guling Pak Malen — another excellent spot for Balinese suckling pig (IDR 80,000–120,000).

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver for the Besakih and Sidemen day trip — IDR 400,000–600,000 for the full day. Dress modestly and bring a sarong for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning yoga session — attend a special 2-hour workshop at Yoga Barn focusing on pranayama (breathwork) and meditation (IDR 200,000–300,000). A meaningful way to consolidate your yoga practice before departing Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's galleries and boutiques one last time. Visit the Neka Art Museum for a comprehensive overview of Balinese painting styles (entry IDR 75,000). Pick up final souvenirs — quality items include silver jewellery, batik fabric, and hand-carved wooden items.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset walk along the Campuhan Ridge. Reflect on the journey and enjoy Ubud's peaceful evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — savour a final Balinese-style breakfast with jaje (rice cakes) and fresh tropical fruit.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sage Restaurant — a popular vegetarian and vegan spot in Ubud (IDR 80,000–130,000).
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Alaya Resort's restaurant or Swept Away at COMO Uma Ubud — elegant atmosphere with Balinese-inspired cuisine (IDR 200,000–400,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to repack, settle any hotel bills, and confirm your departure transport for Day 13. Leave a review for standout experiences to help future travellers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake up early for one last sunrise meditation or a peaceful walk in the hotel garden. Pack remaining belongings and check out of Ubud Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private transfer from Ubud to Ngurah Rai International Airport (approx. 1.5–2 hrs; IDR 200,000–350,000). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Balinese coffee, chocolate, or handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali — carry warm memories of rice terraces, temple ceremonies, ocean sunsets, and yoga sunrises.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — enjoy one last smoothie bowl or nasi goreng.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport — Bebek Tepi Sawah or a local airport restaurant (IDR 80,000–150,000).
meals.dinner: Dinner on the flight or at the departure gate.

day_by_day.notes: Book your airport transfer the night before to ensure punctuality. Bali's traffic can be unpredictable — always allow extra travel time. Check airline baggage allowances if you've purchased souvenirs. Selamat jalan — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Ubud Boutique Stay in Ubud (approx. 1.5 hrs). Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome drink and a relaxing check-in experience. Settle into your villa and take a refreshing dip in the private pool to unwind after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introductory stroll through the charming streets of Ubud town. Visit the iconic Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) for a brief evening look at its illuminated Balinese architecture, then head to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or at airport)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Locavore — Ubud's celebrated farm-to-table fine dining restaurant. Opt for the tasting menu showcasing hyper-local Balinese ingredients with creative modern plating. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and restorative. Ask the hotel concierge to pre-book all upcoming restaurant reservations and experiences upon check-in. Ensure luggage is unpacked and yoga gear is ready for an early morning the next day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session at the hotel's private yoga pavilion or a guided session at the renowned Yoga Barn Ubud (one of Bali's top yoga studios, a short walk or 5-min drive away). Choose a Hatha or Vinyasa class to ease into the trip. Follow with a nourishing in-hotel breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided private tour of the Ubud Monkey Forest (Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary) and the surrounding ancient temples. Continue to the Ubud Art Market for a curated browse of handwoven textiles, silver jewelry, and traditional Balinese crafts. Private guide can assist in selecting authentic premium pieces.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud temple — a mesmerizing traditional Balinese ritual performance held at sunset. Followed by a leisurely dinner in central Ubud.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate à la carte breakfast at the hotel — tropical fruit platters, Balinese black rice porridge, eggs Benedict, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bridges Bali — a stunning riverside restaurant set above the Campuhan River gorge, offering contemporary Asian cuisine and excellent cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique — French-inspired fine dining with Balinese ingredients, set in a romantic garden. One of Ubud's most prestigious dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kecak Dance in advance through the hotel concierge. Bring a light layer for the evening temple performance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the afternoon market and forest visit.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private guided trek through the iconic Tegallalang Rice Terraces at sunrise, when the light is golden and crowds are minimal. A private guide will explain traditional Balinese subak irrigation philosophy. Finish with a coffee stop at a hillside café overlooking the terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tirta Empul Temple — one of Bali's most sacred water temples — for a respectful cultural experience. Observe or participate in the traditional purification ritual (melukat) in the holy spring water pools. Sarongs and guidance provided. Afterward, visit a nearby traditional Balinese healer (Balian) for an optional spiritual consultation arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a 90-minute couples' or solo Balinese massage and spa treatment at the hotel's luxury spa. Conclude with a quiet evening in the villa.

meals.breakfast: Light grab-and-go breakfast from the hotel before the early trek — fresh fruit, granola, and a thermos of Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Swept Away at COMO Shambhala Estate — a serene riverside restaurant offering organic, health-focused cuisine in a breathtaking jungle setting
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining experience arranged by the hotel — a curated 4-course Balinese set menu served on your terrace under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The early morning start (around 5:30 AM) is essential for the best light at Tegallalang. Dress modestly for Tirta Empul (shoulders and knees covered). The hotel can arrange a sarong and sash.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated morning yoga and meditation retreat at The Yoga Barn — attend a 2-hour Yin Yoga or Pranayama breathwork class, followed by a guided 30-minute meditation session. The Yoga Barn offers world-class instructors in a jungle-surrounded studio environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day cultural immersion: visit a local Balinese family compound in a traditional village near Ubud to learn about daily life, offerings (canang sari), and Balinese Hinduism. Continue to a premium silversmithing or batik workshop in the artisan village of Celuk or Mas for a hands-on luxury craft experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Alaya Resort rooftop bar or a similar elevated venue with panoramic Ubud valley views. Then dinner at a top Ubud restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and Balinese herbal jamu shots
meals.lunch: Lunch at Warung Bodag Maliah at Komaneka at Bisma — a cliffside restaurant with stunning Campuhan valley views, serving refined Balinese cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Room4Dessert — an innovative dessert-forward tasting menu experience by world-renowned chef Will Goldfarb, a unique and prestigious Ubud dining event

day_by_day.notes: Book Room4Dessert well in advance as it is one of the most sought-after dining experiences in Bali. The cultural compound visit should be arranged through a reputable local guide to ensure an authentic and respectful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hike to the summit of Mount Batur (Gunung Batur), an active volcano at 1,717 m. Depart from Ubud at approximately 2:00 AM for the 2-hour drive and 2-hour guided hike to reach the summit for a spectacular sunrise above the clouds. A private guide and porter are included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Mount Batur and stop at natural hot spring pools (Toya Devasya Hot Springs) at the volcano's base for a restorative soak with views of the caldera lake. Return to Ubud hotel for rest and recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel — enjoy the pool, a light spa treatment, and a peaceful dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike packed breakfast provided by the guide at the summit — eggs cooked using volcanic steam, sandwiches, fruit, and hot tea (a classic Batur tradition)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the hotel restaurant or a light room service meal upon return — focus on recovery nutrition with protein-rich dishes and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hujan Locale — a relaxed but sophisticated restaurant in Ubud celebrating Indonesian archipelago cuisine with a modern approach, excellent cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur hike requires a very early departure (around 2:00–2:30 AM from Ubud). Arrange private transport the night before. Wear layers as the summit is cool. This is a moderately challenging hike — confirm fitness level with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning after the volcano hike. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely in-room breakfast, and spend time at the hotel pool or garden. Optional: a gentle restorative yoga class at the hotel pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) — an 11th-century archaeological site and sacred temple just outside Ubud. Continue to the Pura Kehen temple in Bangli — one of Bali's most impressive and less-touristy Hindu temples, set on a hillside with tiered shrines and ancient frangipani trees.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a full luxury spa evening at the hotel — begin with a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub, followed by a 2-hour Royal Balinese massage using warm coconut oil and aromatic spices. End with a flower petal bath in your villa.

meals.breakfast: Lavish in-room breakfast — full tropical spread with fresh coconut, papaya, dragon fruit, Balinese coffee, and a hot cooked option of your choice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sari Organik — a beloved organic farm-to-table restaurant set in the middle of rice fields, accessible via a scenic walk through the paddies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alaya Ubud's Plantation Restaurant — elegant open-air dining with panoramic rice terrace views and an extensive menu of refined Indonesian and international dishes

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately gentle day to recover from the volcano hike. Don't over-schedule — the luxury of time is part of the premium experience. Dress modestly for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Ubud to Seminyak/Canggu area (approx. 1.5 hrs) for a beach day. Check into a luxury day-use suite or beach club. Begin the morning with a private surf lesson on the gentler waves of Batu Bolong Beach in Canggu with a professional instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Finns Beach Club or Potato Head Beach Club — two of Bali's most iconic luxury beach clubs, offering private cabanas, infinity pools, and premium bottle service. Enjoy the warm July sun (avg. 25°C) and the vibrant atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach at La Plancha Bali — famous for its colorful bean bags directly on the sand and spectacular sunsets. Then transfer back to Ubud or stay in the beach area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure — light and energizing with açaí bowls, fresh fruit, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Potato Head Beach Club — Mediterranean-inspired sharing plates, fresh seafood, and signature cocktails by the infinity pool
meals.dinner: Dinner at Metis Restaurant in Seminyak — a legendary French-Mediterranean fine dining restaurant set in a stunning colonial villa with lush tropical gardens

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private transfer to the beach area in advance. If preferring to stay closer to Ubud, Balangan Beach or Padang Padang offer a more secluded, premium beach experience with less drive time. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the hotel terrace or at The Yoga Barn. Follow with a private Balinese cooking class held in a traditional compound kitchen near Ubud — learn to prepare 5–6 signature dishes including satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding, with a market visit to source ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum — the flamboyant former home and studio of Spanish-Balinese artist Don Antonio Blanco, filled with his romantic and surrealist masterpieces. Continue to explore the galleries and artisan studios along Jalan Hanoman and Jalan Monkey Forest.
day_by_day.evening: Private romantic candlelit dinner experience set up by the hotel in a secluded rice field or garden location — a bespoke setup with a personal butler, curated 5-course menu, and live traditional Balinese music.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast at the hotel — banana, dates, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the morning cooking class as your lunch — a unique and rewarding farm-to-table experience
meals.dinner: Private bespoke candlelit dinner in a scenic outdoor setting arranged by the hotel concierge — a signature luxury Bali experience

day_by_day.notes: The private rice field dinner must be arranged at least 2–3 days in advance with the hotel. This is one of the most memorable experiences of the trip — confirm dietary preferences and any special occasion details.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to East Bali — depart early for the Besakih Temple (Mother Temple of Bali), Bali's largest and most sacred Hindu temple complex, dramatically set on the slopes of Mount Agung. A private guide will provide deep cultural and spiritual context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the serene Tirta Gangga Water Palace — a royal garden with ornamental ponds, stone sculptures, and stepping-stone paths, surrounded by rice terraces. Take a refreshing dip in the spring-fed pools. Drive back toward Ubud via the scenic coastal road through Klungkung.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Ubud for a relaxed evening. Visit a traditional Balinese healer (optional, if not done earlier) or enjoy a sound healing/crystal bowl meditation session arranged by the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before departure — fuel up for a full day of exploration
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming local warung in the Tirta Gangga area — fresh grilled fish, lawar, and steamed rice with a view of the rice paddies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Naughty Nuri's Warung — a beloved Ubud institution famous for its slow-cooked pork ribs and potent martinis. A quintessential Bali experience even at the premium level.

day_by_day.notes: Besakih Temple requires modest dress and a sarong (provided at the entrance). Hire a knowledgeable private guide to navigate the complex. The round trip to East Bali is approximately 3–4 hours of driving total — depart by 7:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive morning yoga and wellness retreat day — begin with a 90-minute Kundalini yoga class at The Yoga Barn, followed by a guided pranayama and meditation workshop. Afterward, enjoy a Jamu herbal wellness consultation and personalized herbal tonic preparation at a local Balinese apothecary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic private cycling tour through the rural villages, rice fields, and jungle paths north of Ubud (Tegallalang–Kintamani route). E-bikes available for a more leisurely premium experience. Stop at local family compounds and a traditional palm sugar production facility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a sunset cocktail hour at the hotel bar. Enjoy a quiet, indulgent evening with a private in-villa dinner and a late-night stargazing session from your terrace or pool area.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga breakfast at the hotel — protein-rich smoothie bowls, poached eggs, avocado, and Balinese herbal tea
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch provided during the cycling tour — local delicacies, fresh fruit, artisanal snacks, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: In-villa private dinner — a curated menu of Balinese specialties served by a personal butler with a selection from the hotel's premium wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The cycling tour difficulty can be adjusted to your fitness level. E-bikes make the experience accessible and enjoyable even in warm weather. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light rain jacket as afternoon showers can occasionally occur in July.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Nusa Penida (approx. 1.5 hrs to Sanur harbor + 45-min fast boat). Arrive at Nusa Penida for a private full-day island tour. First stop: the iconic Kelingking Beach viewpoint — one of the most breathtaking coastal vistas in all of Indonesia, with dramatic limestone cliffs and turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Crystal Bay — a calm, crystal-clear bay ideal for snorkeling with vibrant coral reefs and the chance to spot Mola Mola (ocean sunfish) in season. Private snorkeling equipment and guide included. Visit the natural pool at Angel's Billabong and the dramatic arch at Broken Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return fast boat to Sanur and private transfer back to Ubud. Arrive in time for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — light and energizing
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside warung on Nusa Penida — grilled fish, prawn satay, and cold Bintang beer with an ocean view
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aperitif Restaurant Ubud — a glamorous, art deco-inspired fine dining venue offering an exceptional tasting menu with wine pairing, one of Bali's most prestigious restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Book the fast boat in advance through the hotel concierge. The Nusa Penida day trip is long (depart by 7:00 AM) but highly rewarding. Bring motion sickness medication if needed for the boat crossing. The Kelingking Beach descent is steep and optional.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning of yoga — a special 2-hour private one-on-one yoga session tailored to your practice level, held in the hotel's private pavilion or a scenic outdoor platform overlooking the jungle or rice fields. Conclude with a guided 30-minute journaling and intention-setting meditation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon for personal time — revisit favorite spots in Ubud, do final shopping for premium Balinese souvenirs (handmade jewelry, fine batik, artisanal ceramics, organic skincare products). Visit the Gaya Ceramic Arts Center or the Threads of Life textile gallery for unique, high-quality keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury spa journey at the hotel — a 3-hour 'Royal Bali' spa package including a full-body Lulur scrub, floral bath, Balinese massage, and reflexology. End the evening with a celebratory farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip or a new discovery.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — order freely from the full menu, savor every dish
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beloved Ubud café — try Kafe Ubud or Clear Café for healthy, organic dishes in a relaxed garden setting
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Locavore or Mozaic (return visit to your favorite fine dining experience from the trip) — celebrate the journey with a full tasting menu and premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to slow down and be present. Avoid over-scheduling. Allow time to reflect on the journey. Confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge — arrange airport transfer time for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise moment — wake early for one last quiet sunrise walk through the Ubud rice fields or a gentle 30-minute meditation on the hotel terrace. Enjoy a peaceful last breakfast at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out from Ubud Boutique Stay. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (approx. 1.5 hrs). Arrive with ample time before departure. If time permits, browse the airport's premium duty-free shops for last-minute Balinese coffee, chocolate, or artisanal gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry the tranquility, warmth, and spirit of the island home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a mindful, unhurried meal to close the journey. Choose your favorite dishes from the past 13 days.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop at a café in Seminyak if the route allows — Revolver Espresso or Watercress Café for a premium coffee and snack
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in, security, and immigration. Request a late check-out from the hotel if your flight is in the afternoon or evening — most luxury properties accommodate this. Ensure all purchases are properly packed and declared if necessary.
